messages:
maria: Heads up — trying to wire Azure Key Vault (AKV) with a VM system-assigned MSI across subscriptions for our envelope-encryption flow. When the VM in sub-B calls wrapKey on a key in vault in sub-A we get 403. Anyone seen cross-subscription MSI authz quirks?

jack: Are the subscriptions in the same tenant? MSI identities are AAD objects — cross-tenant won't work. If same tenant, RBAC should be fine.

maria: Yes same tenant. We gave the VM's identity the crypto role on the key resource but still 403. Using `az role assignment create --assignee <principalId> --role \"Key Vault Crypto User\" --scope /subscriptions/AAA/resourceGroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/my-vault/keys/my-key`

olivia: A couple gotchas: (1) Key Vault has two permission models — Access Policies vs Azure RBAC. Make sure your vault is set to use Azure RBAC for keys (permission model = \"Azure RBAC\"). (2) Role assignment propagation can take a minute. (3) Token caching: MSI token TTL may cause old token to be used — restart the service or force new token.

dave: Also check the role scope — if you assigned at the vault level vs key version level. For wrap/unwrap you need the crypto key permissions. Try assigning at the specific key scope to rule out scope mismatch.

maria: Vault is on \"Azure RBAC\" mode. We assigned at vault scope. Restarted VM, still 403. Sample error: `{"error":{"code":"Forbidden","message":"Access denied to key for wrapKey"}}`

sec_bot: Quick checklist: enable diagnostic logs (AuditEvent) on the Key Vault -> send to Log Analytics or Event Hub. That will show authorization checks and principal id used. Also confirm principalId in role assignment matches the MSI principal, not the VM resource id.

jack: Can you paste the role assignment output? `az role assignment list --assignee <principalId> --scope <keyScope>`

maria: Output shows the role assigned to principalId X on vault scope. Diagnostic log shows the request principal as `spn:0`? (weird) and correlation id.

olivia: If the diagnostic shows `spn:` or an app id that doesn't match the system-assigned identity, check whether the process is using a user-assigned identity instead. System-assigned MSI looks like a service principal guid. Also check local code — are you requesting token for resource `https://vault.azure.net`? Wrong audience will produce auth but insufficient scope.

maria: We're using Azure SDK default, it calls `https://vault.azure.net/.default`. Confirmed.

dave: Another edge: cross-subscription network restrictions — if vault firewall is enabled and only allows certain VNets, a VM in another subscription but same tenant may still be blocked. Firewall error looks like 403 too. Check firewall & private endpoints.

maria: Vault has a private endpoint. The VM talks over peering to that vnet. Peering appears fine.

jack: Two more troubleshooting steps: (1) Use `az account get-access-token --resource https://vault.azure.net` from the VM to see the token and principal. (2) Try `curl` to the Key Vault key operation with that token to replicate.

maria: Did the `get-access-token`, principal matches the MSI principalId. Token audience correct. Replayed curl, same 403.

olivia: In that case: check whether the key is an HSM-protected key (managed HSM) vs software key. Managed HSM uses slightly different RBAC roles. Also confirm the role you assigned is one of: `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` or `Key Vault Crypto User` — try `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` at key scope.

maria: Key is a normal Key Vault key (not managed HSM). We switched to `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` and after propagation the wrapKey succeeded :tada:.

sec_bot: Notes for docs: common failure modes -> permission model mismatch (Access Policies vs RBAC), role scope mismatch, token caching, vault firewall/private endpoint, key type differences, cross-tenant impossibility, and role propagation delay.

dave: For our envelope encryption rotation plan: rotate key by creating a new key version, update the envelope key wrapper on the service to use the new key version id, and invalidate caches. Use AKV key rotation policy where supported and emit an event on version creation to our rotation job (Event Grid subscription on `Microsoft.KeyVault.Vaults/keys/write`).

maria: One more subtlety: when rotating, remember existing ciphertexts use old wrapped DEKs. Keep old key versions around until rewrap process completes. Also for audit & compliance save key rotation metadata in our DB (key id -> rotation timestamp, actor principal).

jack: For incident response, add an alert: if a key is disabled or someone changes access model, send high-sev page. Diagnostic settings + Azure Activity Logs -> Monitor Alert with condition on `OperationName` and `Status` should cover it.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update runbook with the checklist and the `az` snippets. If anyone wants to pair on the Event Grid trigger for rotation rewrap job ping me.

infra-bot: deploy:config - updated runbooks/akv-msi-checklist.md (PR #432)

maria: Added notes and the exact `az role assignment` command we used. Leaving this thread open for 24h in case anything else pops up.
